beats.title: Intro: The Exam Question
beats.says: Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14. The answer is 3n plus 2, and by the end of this video, you'll do questions like this in under 30 seconds.

beats.title: The Method: Three Quick Steps
beats.says: Step one: find the difference. It goes up by 3 each time, so the nth term starts with 3n. Step two: write out the 3 times table: 3, 6, 9, 12. Step three: compare. Each term is 2 more than the times table, so add 2. So the nth term is 3n plus 2.
beats.key: Difference → that times n. Then compare with the times table and adjust.

beats.title: Why It Works: The Dot Pattern
beats.says: Here's why that works. Picture the sequence as dots: 5, then 8, then 11, then 14. Each step adds 3 new dots, which is the 3n. And there are 2 dots that are always there from the start, which is the plus 2. So the dots are 3n plus 2.
beats.key: The difference is what gets added each time. The adjustment is what was there at the start.

beats.title: Check It
beats.says: Always check with the first term. Put n equals 1 into 3n plus 2: 3 plus 2 is 5. That's the first term, so it's right.
beats.onScreen: Worked: n = 1: 3 × 1 + 2 = 5 ✓ // matches the first term | n = 2: 3 × 2 + 2 = 8 ✓
beats.key: Check by putting n = 1 back in.

beats.title: Going Down: Negative Differences
beats.says: If the sequence goes down, the difference is negative. 20, 17, 14, 11 goes down by 3, so it's minus 3n. The minus 3 times table is minus 3, minus 6, minus 9, minus 12. Each term is 23 more, so add 23. So the nth term is minus 3n plus 23.
beats.key: Going down? The difference is negative, so start with −3n.

beats.title: Using the nth Term
beats.says: Once you have the nth term, you can find any term. The 50th term of 3n plus 2 is 3 times 50, plus 2, which is 152. And to check if a number is in the sequence, set it equal and solve. Is 100 in it? 3n plus 2 equals 100 gives n equals 32.67. That's not a whole number, so no.
beats.onScreen: Worked: 50th term = 3 × 50 + 2 = 152 | 3n + 2 = 100 // is 100 in it? | n = 32.67 // not a whole number | 100 is not in the sequence ✗
beats.key: Is it in the sequence? Solve: a whole number n means yes.

beats.title: Exam Tips: Common Mistakes
beats.says: The mistakes that lose marks: writing n plus 3 instead of 3n, forgetting the minus sign when the sequence goes down, and not checking with the first term.
beats.onScreen: Worked: ✗ n + 3 // it's 3n: the difference goes in front | ✗ 3n + 23 for 20, 17, 14… // going down: −3n | ✓ difference · times table · adjust · check

beats.title: Your Turn: Answer
beats.says: It goes up by 7, so it starts 7n. The 7 times table is 7, 14, 21, 28. Each term is 3 less, so it's 7n minus 3. If you got that, you've got it.
